messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 503 errors and latency on inference-us-east-1 detected (5+% errors over 3m). Paging primary on-call.
Maya L: Acked pager, creating quick kickoff. War room: https://meet.redwood/warroom/1760860800
Maya L: Incident lead: @Santiago R. Scribe: @Priya K. Primary on-call: @Jared M.
Santiago R: I'm taking lead. Quick summary: generation/chat routes showing spikes in 95p latency and 503s. Traffic grows in us-east and spillover to eu-west. Initial suspicion: kv-cache write contention / eviction.
Priya K: Joining war room, creating incident notes doc.
Jared M: Acked. Running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` and `nvidia-smi` to check GPU saturation.
Niko: FYI, we had load-testing in staging earlier that exercised cache eviction; logs showed OOMs for flusher process around 09:55 UTC.
ops-bot: Autoscaler event: added 2 instances in us-east at 2026-03-17T10:03:21Z (asg-inference-us-east-2). Scaling didn't fully mitigate errors.
Maya L: Customer impact: intermittent 503s and higher latency for hosted API in US-East; some EU requests routed via US-East may be affected. No reported data corruption.
Maya L: Draft status page update below — quick review please.
Maya L: ```
Status: Investigating
Summary: We're investigating elevated error rates and latency affecting the hosted inference API in US-East. Some requests may receive 503 responses. Engineers are actively investigating and mitigating.
Advice: Retry with exponential backoff. For Dedicated customers, we'll DM account teams with details.
Impact: Partial degradation of generation/chat endpoints in US-East (possible spillover).
ETA: TBD
``` 
Santiago R: Add that we're performing controlled traffic failovers for non-pinned routes and pausing cache writes as an interim mitigation.
Maya L: Updated. Who can run the failover and verify kv-cache consistency? @Jared M?
Jared M: I can initiate a controlled failover for non-pinned traffic. Plan: pause cache flusher, run `scripts/region_failover.sh --from us-east --to us-west --dry-run` then cut if checks pass.
Priya K: I'll prep DMs for Dedicated and enterprise accounts; also assemble a customer impact list to attach to status updates.
Maya L: ops-runbook: Step 1 pause cache writes, Step 2 failover non-pinned traffic, Step 3 scale further if needed. Escalation to secondary in 10m if unresolved.
incident-bot: Reminder: escalation window in 10m if unacknowledged by secondary.
Santiago R: Running health checks now. `scripts/health_check.sh --region us-east` in progress.
Jared M: Dry-run completed successfully. Starting pause of cache flushers now.
Niko: Adding a temporary metric to watch: prefix-miss rate, kv-write latency, 503 count per route.
Maya L: Posting status update now. Priya, send private DMs to active enterprise contacts.
Priya K: Sent private DMs to five enterprise owners. Also created a draft email for Dedicated customers with mitigation steps and ETA placeholder.
Jared M: Failover executed at 10:08 UTC for non-pinned traffic. Routes updated. Monitoring for token-per-second and error-rate.
ops-bot: Failover action logged (action_id: ff-1760860800-1). Cache flushers paused.
Maya L: Early results: error-rate down from 5% to ~1.3%, 95p latency trending down. Still watching for residual spikes.
Santiago R: If KV consistency checks look good after 15m of stability, we'll unpause writers and keep mitigations in place for 1 hour.
Maya L: Assigning follow-ups: postmortem owner @Maya L, root-cause lead @Niko. Incident remains open until stable for 1 hour.
Priya K: Scribe notes posted to incident tracker with timeline and customer DM copies. I'll keep updating the status page edits.
Jared M: I'll stay on the war room for the next 30 minutes to watch the metrics and handle rollback if needed.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: status -> MONITORING at 2026-03-17T10:18:34Z. Participants recorded: Maya L, Santiago R, Priya K, Jared M, Niko, ops-bot.
Maya L: Closing kickoff thread — we'll reconvene for a mid-incident review in 30 minutes unless critical changes occur.
